questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay related to the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. Young people spend a lot of time on the Internet. However, they are sometimes unable to recognize false information on the Internet, judge the reliability of online information sources, or tell real news stories from fake ones.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
It has become a common phenomenon that young people spend a great deal of time online, yet many of them struggle to tell trustworthy information from falsehood. As the passage notes, they are often unable to recognize false information, judge the reliability of online sources, or distinguish real news from fake stories. This deficiency in digital judgment, though easily overlooked, deserves our serious attention.

The consequences are far from trivial. Misled by fabricated news, young people may form distorted views of the world, make ill-informed decisions, and even spread rumours unknowingly. Since their critical-thinking skills are still developing, they are especially vulnerable to eye-catching yet groundless claims that circulate rapidly across social media.

To address this issue, concerted efforts are needed. First and foremost, schools should offer media-literacy courses that teach students how to verify facts and trace information back to its source. Meanwhile, online platforms ought to strengthen fact-checking and clearly label questionable content. Finally, young people themselves should cultivate the habit of cross-checking a story against several reliable sources before believing or sharing it. Only in this way can they navigate the digital world wisely.

transcript.text: W: Hi, David. I haven't seen you in class for almost two weeks. We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.
transcript.zh: W: 嗨，戴维。我快两周没在课堂上见到你了。我们还以为你提早休假去哪里了呢。

transcript.text: M: Hi, Sarah. Well, it's a bit of a long story I'm afraid. I got a throat infection last week and had to go to the hospital to get some antibiotics as I really wasn't getting any better.
transcript.zh: M: 嗨，莎拉。唉，说来话长。我上周喉咙感染了，因为病情实在不见好转，不得不去医院开了一些抗生素。

transcript.zh: M: 更糟糕的是，我偏偏摔在了四个九年级女生面前。简直丢脸丢到家了。而且，我包里的笔记本电脑也摔坏了。

transcript.text: W: No, what a complete catastrophe! Is the laptop still under warranty? If it is, then you can easily send it back to the manufacturer, and they'll send you a brand-new one for free surely.
transcript.zh: W: 天啊，这真是彻头彻尾的灾难！笔记本电脑还在保修期内吗？如果是的话，你就可以很方便地寄回给厂家，他们肯定会免费给你寄一台全新的。

transcript.text: M: The warranty ran out three days before I broke it. And all my essays are in there, and I need to hand them in before we break for the Christmas holidays.
transcript.zh: M: 保修期在我摔坏它的前三天就过了。我所有的论文都在里面，而且我必须在放圣诞假之前把它们交上去。

transcript.text: W: Listen, I have the number of a really good, affordable computer repair shop at home. My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles. Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop, and you can have some tea and cookies too.
transcript.zh: W: 听我说，我家里有一家又好又实惠的电脑维修店的电话。我爸爸以前找过这个人，他简直能创造奇迹。我们回我家吧，我们可以给维修店打电话，你还可以喝点茶、吃点饼干。

transcript.text: M: Wow, thanks, Sarah! That would be great! Let me just call my mom and let her know I'll be home a little bit later.
transcript.zh: M: 哇，谢谢你，莎拉！那太好了！我先给我妈妈打个电话，跟她说一声我会晚一点回家。

questions.stem: What does Sarah think David was doing for the last two weeks?

options.text: He was busy writing his essays.
He was fighting a throat infection.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.信号：thought 引出的"我们以为" 。答案信号是表"猜测"的 We thought you had disappeared on holiday early——题干问的正是 Sarah "think" 什么，录音里对…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 盗用了录音里 David 自述去医院的情节（had to go to the hospital），但那是"实际发生"且由 David 本人后说出来的，并非 Sarah "以为"的内容；题干问的是 Sarah 的猜测，故 B 答非所问。 借用原文：all my essays are in there
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 盗用了录音后半 all my essays are in there（论文都在电脑里）的 essays 一词，制造"听到 essays 就选"的诱惑；但那是讲电脑坏了的麻烦，根本不是 Sarah 对"这两周在做什么"的猜测。 借用原文：I got a throat infection last week
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 盗用 David 自述的 I got a throat infection last week（得了喉咙感染），是真实发生的病情；但题干要的是 Sarah "以为"的内容，Sarah 当时以为他在度假，并不知道他生病，故 D 张冠李戴、答非所问。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（disappeared on holiday early ↔ He was enjoying his holiday. 去度假 = 享受假期）

questions.evidenceText: We thought you had disappeared on holiday early or something.

questions.stem: What happened to David on his way back from the hospital?

options.text: He slipped on ice and fell.
He was laughed at by some girls.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：And, on the way back from the hospital, I slipped on some ice and fell and then had to go to the hospital to get an X-ray because I basically thought I broke my wrist, although, thankfully, it's not broken.信号：题干同序短语 on the way back 直接对位 。答案信号是录音里与题干几乎同词的 on the way back from the hospital——题目限定"回来的路上"，录音正好用同一短语领起这件事，…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A 盗用录音 I basically thought I broke my wrist 里的 broke my wrist，但紧跟着是 although, thankfully, it's not broken（其实没断）。选项只取了"以为断了"、漏掉了否定反转，与原文相反，故错。 借用原文：get some antibiotics
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 盗用录音 get some antibiotics 里的 antibiotics 一词，制造熟词诱惑；但录音只说去医院拿抗生素，从未提"丢了药"，属无中生有，且与"路上发生的事"无关。 借用原文：I managed to fall right in front of four girls from the ninth grade
optionAnalysis.D: 答非所问：D 盗用录音 fall right in front of four girls 的"被女生看到/笑"情节，听上去确有其事；但那是 To make things worse 之后追加的另一桩糗事，题干问的是"回来路上发生了什么"，对应的是滑倒，D 答非所问。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I slipped on some ice and fell ↔ He slipped on ice and fell. 几乎原样对应的动作）

questions.evidenceText: And, on the way back from the hospital, I slipped on some ice and fell and then had to go to the hospital to get an X-ray because I basically thought I broke my wrist, although, thankfully, it's not broken.

questions.stem: What does Sarah say they should do with the damaged computer?

options.text: Turn to her father for help.
Call the repair shop to fix it.
Replace it with a brand-new one.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：Listen, I have the number of a really good, affordable computer repair shop at home. My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles. Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop.信号：Let's… 之前被否掉、之后才是定案 。前文 P7 先提"在保修期就退给厂家换新机"，但 P8 一句 The warranty ran out three days before I broke it（保修过期了）…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 盗用录音 My dad has used this guy before 里的 dad，制造"听到 dad 就选"的诱惑；但录音只是说"她爸以前找过这家维修店"，用来佐证店靠谱，并非"向她爸求助"，故 A 偷换概念。 借用原文：you can easily send it back to the manufacturer
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 盗用录音 send it back to the manufacturer 里的 manufacturer，听起来像方案之一；但 P8 的 The warranty ran out（保修已过期）已把这条路堵死，它是被否掉的方案，非最终决定。 借用原文：they'll send you a brand-new one for free surely
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D 盗用录音 they'll send you a brand-new one 里的 brand-new，最诱人；但"免费换新机"的前提是 Is the laptop still under warranty，而保修已过期，这个方案随之作废，故 D 与原文相反。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（call the repair shop ↔ Call the repair shop to fix it. 打电话给维修店 = 找维修店修）

questions.evidenceText: Listen, I have the number of a really good, affordable computer repair shop at home. My dad has used this guy before and he can work miracles. Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop.

questions.stem: What does Sarah say she is going to do?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop, and you can have some tea and cookies too.信号：Let's / you can have 引出的主动招待 。答案信号是 Sarah 结尾的邀约句 you can have some tea and cookies too——you can have 引出她要为 D…

optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：A 盗用录音 all my essays are in there 的 essays，听上去像"帮他取回论文"；但 Sarah 提供的是"打电话找维修店修电脑"，retrieve essays（取回论文）是修好后才可能的结果，录音并未说她要去取论文，属过度推断。 借用原文：Let's go back to my house
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 借"去她家、提到她 dad"的语境（My dad has used this guy before）让人联想"见家长"；但录音只说回她家打电话、吃茶点，从没提"introduce David to her parents（引见给父母）"，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D 把录音 Let's go back to my house（回我家）的方向偷偷反过来，写成 Accompany David to his home.（陪他回他家）。go back to my house 指"去 Sarah 家"，与"to his home"正好相反，属方向/地点偷换。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（you can have some tea and cookies too ↔ Offer David some refreshments. 茶和饼干 = refreshments（茶点））

questions.evidenceText: Let's go back to my house and we can call the repair shop, and you can have some tea and cookies too.

transcript.text: M: Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk. With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.
transcript.zh: M: 欢迎收听本周的《图书谈》。今天和我一起做节目的是海蒂·布朗，她是一位历史学家，已经写了五本广受评论界好评的军事史著作。

transcript.text: W: Thanks for having me, John. I'm so excited to talk about my latest book, which was published last month.
transcript.zh: W: 谢谢你邀请我，约翰。我非常高兴能聊聊我的最新著作，这本书上个月刚刚出版。

transcript.text: M: So this book is a novel, your first attempt at that genre. I thought it was a bit of a departure for you.
transcript.zh: M: 所以，这本书是一部小说，是你第一次尝试这一体裁。我觉得这对你来说是一个不小的转变。

transcript.text: W: I'd say it's a major departure as it's not just a work of fiction. It's set 200 years in the future.
transcript.zh: W: 我会说这是一次很大的转变，因为它不只是一部虚构作品，故事还设定在两百年后的未来。

transcript.text: M: Right. So how did that happen? You spent three decades writing about the past and focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries. And now you're speculating about the future.
transcript.zh: M: 好。那么这是怎么发生的？你花了三十年时间写过去的历史，重点关注十八世纪和十九世纪。现在却开始推测未来。

transcript.text: W: Well, after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives during battle, I just started wondering about other facets of their lives, especially their personal lives.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，多年来研究士兵并记录他们在战斗中的生活之后，我开始思考他们生活中的其他方面，尤其是他们的私人生活。

transcript.text: M: I can see that. Your novel is about soldiers and it focuses on their relationships, especially the bond between sons and mothers and men and their wives.
transcript.zh: M: 我能理解。你的小说写的是士兵，重点讲述他们之间的关系，尤其是儿子与母亲之间的感情，以及男人与妻子之间的联系。

transcript.text: W: Yes. That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history. I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.
transcript.zh: W: 是的。我最初打算再写一本历史书时，就产生了这个关注点。我先研究士兵真实的私人生活，研读他们寄回家的信件。

transcript.text: M: So how did that history book become a novel?
transcript.zh: M: 那么，这本历史书后来是怎么变成小说的？

transcript.text: W: Well, I realized that the historical record was incomplete. So I'd either have to leave a lot of gaps or make a lot more assumptions than a historian should.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，我意识到历史记录并不完整。所以，我要么得留下许多空白，要么就得做出远超历史学家应有程度的大量推断。

transcript.text: M: But why write a novel set in the future when your credentials are perfect for a historical novel? As a historian, any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility.
transcript.zh: M: 但既然你的资历非常适合写历史小说，为什么要写一部以未来为背景的小说呢？作为一名历史学家，无论你写什么历史小说，都会很有可信度。

transcript.text: W: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.
transcript.zh: W: 我觉得创作过去的题材束缚太多了，好像我写的东西必须是事实，而不能是虚构。但写未来让我有更多自由去想象和创造。

transcript.text: M: Well, having read your book, I'm glad you made that choice to move into fiction.
transcript.zh: M: 读过你的书之后，我很高兴你做出了转向小说创作的选择。

questions.stem: What does the man say about the woman?

options.text: She is a critic of works on military affairs.
She is an acclaimed hostess of Book Talk.
She is a researcher of literary genres.
She is a historian of military history.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.信号：主持人开场介绍嘉宾的应答位 。信号是开场白里主持人介绍来宾的那句 With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian…——访谈类对话，嘉宾身份就在主持人 "今天的嘉宾是…" 这句里点出…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：critic of works on military affairs 借了原文的 military 一词，但原文说她 has written five … books（她是写书的作者），不是 "评论他人作品的评论家"，身份对不上。 借用原文：Welcome to this week's episode of Book Talk
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：hostess of Book Talk 盗用了开场的节目名 Book Talk，但主持节目的是男方（he），女方是受邀嘉宾，把主持人身份安到了女方头上。 借用原文：your first attempt at that genre
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：researcher of literary genres 里的 genres 蹭了后文谈体裁的内容，但原文明确说她是 a historian，不是 "文学体裁研究者"，身份被偷换。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history ↔ She is a historian of military history. 把长定语压缩成 historian of military history）

questions.evidenceText: With me today is Heidi Brown, a historian who has written five critically acclaimed books about military history.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her newly published book?

options.text: It is about the military history of Europe.
It is set in the 18th and 19th centuries.
It is her fifth book of military history.
It is a war novel set in the future.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：I'd say it's a major departure as it's not just a work of fiction. It's set 200 years in the future.信号：被问者亲口描述新书的应答句 。信号是女方自己介绍新书的那句 It's set 200 years in the future——题目问 "woman say about her book"，落点就在被问者亲口说书的特…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：military history of Europe 蹭了开场说她写 military history 的话，但那指她过去五本书，新书是面向未来的小说；且原文从未提 Europe。 借用原文：focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：set in the 18th and 19th centuries 直接盗用主持人那句 focusing on the 18th and 19th centuries，但那说的是她 "过去三十年研究的年代"，新书恰恰相反，是设定在 future。 借用原文：has written five critically acclaimed books about military history
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：her fifth book of military history 盗用了 five … books about military history 里的 five，但 five 是她此前史书的数量，新书是新出的小说，不是 "第五本军事史"。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a work of fiction ↔ a war novel fiction=novel，结合前文军人题材即 war novel）

questions.evidenceText: I'd say it's a major departure as it's not just a work of fiction. It's set 200 years in the future.

questions.stem: What did the woman do before writing her new book?

options.text: She visited soldiers' wives and mothers.
She conducted surveys of many soldiers.
She met a large number of soldiers in person.
She looked into the personal lives of soldiers.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history. I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.信号：被问者讲自己怎么起步的应答句 。信号是女方自述研究起点的那句 I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives——题目问她写书前做了什么，落点就在被问者…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：visited soldiers' wives and mothers 盗用第7段 the bond between sons and mothers and men and their wives 里的 mothers、wives，但那说的是小说写的关系，不是她去 "探访" 了这些人，动作无中生有。 借用原文：studying their letters home
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：conducted surveys of many soldiers 与原文 studying their letters home 方式不符——她是研读士兵的家书，不是 "对众多士兵做问卷调查"，调研方式被偷换。 借用原文：after years of researching soldiers and chronicling their lives
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：met a large number of soldiers in person 借了原文反复出现的 soldiers，但她是 studying their letters home（读信），原文从未说她 "当面见了大量士兵"，in person 与数量都是加出来的。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（researching soldiers' actual personal lives ↔ looked into the personal lives of soldiers researching=looked into，词序调整）

questions.evidenceText: That focus came about when I still intended to write another book of history. I started by researching soldiers' actual personal lives, studying their letters home.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her writing history books?

options.text: She doesn't have much freedom for imagination.
It is not easy to make her readers believe in her.
It is difficult to attract young readers.
She has to combine fact with fiction.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P12）：I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.信号：感受词 felt too constrained + 转折 but 。信号有两处：一是被问者直陈感受的 I felt too constrained working with the past（写过去让我太受束缚），…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：make her readers believe in her 蹭了主持人那句 any historical novel you write would have a lot of credibility 的 credibility，但那是主持人讲 "你写历史小说会很可信"，不是她说 "难让读者相信她"，张冠李戴且意思相反。 借用原文：what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：difficult to attract young readers 里的 "young readers" 原文从头到尾没出现，她谈的是写作自由问题，跟 "吸引年轻读者" 毫无关系。
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：combine fact with fiction 直接搬来原文的 fact as opposed to fiction，但原文是 "事实 与 虚构 相对立"，且她觉得写史书时只能要 fact 不能要 fiction，根本不是 "把事实与虚构结合"。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I felt too constrained working with the past ↔ She doesn't have much freedom for imagination. constrained=没有多少自由，肯否定转换）

questions.evidenceText: I felt too constrained working with the past, like what I wrote needed to be fact as opposed to fiction, but writing about the future gave me more freedom to imagine, to invent.

transcript.text: Whether it's in the hands of animated polar bears or Santa Claus, there's one thing you'll find in nearly all ads for Coca-Cola: the characteristic glass bottle. Most Americans don't drink soda out of the glass bottles seen in Coke's ads anymore. But this week, the company is celebrating a century of the bottle that's been sold in more than 200 countries.
transcript.zh: 无论是由动画片中的北极熊还是圣诞老人拿着，在几乎所有可口可乐的广告中，你都会看到同一样东西：那只独具特色的玻璃瓶。如今，大多数美国人已经不再用可口可乐广告中出现的玻璃瓶喝汽水了。但本周，这家公司正在庆祝这种已在全球200多个国家销售的瓶子问世一百周年。

transcript.text: Flash back to 1915, when a bottle of Coca-Cola cost just a nickel. As the soft drink gained in popularity, it faced a growing number of competitors—counterfeits even trying to copy Coke's logo. So, according to Coca-Cola historian Ted Ryan, the company decided to come up with packaging that couldn't be duplicated.
transcript.zh: 回到1915年，那时一瓶可口可乐只要5美分。随着这种软饮料越来越受欢迎，它面临的竞争者也越来越多，甚至还有仿冒品试图复制可口可乐的标志。因此，据可口可乐历史学家特德·瑞安介绍，公司决定设计一种无法仿制的包装。

transcript.text: A product request was sent to eight different glass makers. Workers at the Root Glass Company got the request and began flipping through the encyclopedia at the local library, landing on cocoa seed. Though cocoa seed is not an ingredient of the soda, they designed their bottle based on the seed's shape and large middle. It won over Coke executives in Atlanta and would go on to receive its own trademark, spur collections and earn Coca-Cola an iconic image that made it part of American culture for a century.
transcript.zh: 公司向八家不同的玻璃制造商发出了一份产品设计要求。鲁特玻璃公司的工人收到要求后，开始在当地的图书馆翻阅百科全书，最后注意到了可可种子。虽然可可种子并不是这种汽水的原料，但他们根据种子的形状和中部较大的特点设计了瓶子。这一设计赢得了亚特兰大可口可乐公司高管的认可，后来还获得了自己的商标，推动了收藏热潮，并为可口可乐赢得了一个具有标志性的形象，使其在一个世纪里成为美国文化的一部分。

transcript.text: It was 100 years ago this week that the bottle earned a patent. By World War II, Coke bottle sales had ballooned into billions. Americans mostly consume Coke out of aluminum or plastic today, but the glass bottle remains a symbol of America that's readily recognized around the world.
transcript.zh: 就在本周之前的一百年前，这种瓶子获得了专利。到第二次世界大战时，可口可乐瓶装产品的销量已经达到数十亿瓶。如今，美国人饮用可口可乐时主要使用铝罐或塑料瓶，但这种玻璃瓶仍然是美国的象征，在世界各地都很容易被认出。

transcript.text: Research shows that a few moments of conversation with a stranger creates a measurable improvement in mood. But most of us are reluctant to start these conversations because we presume the opposite.
transcript.zh: 研究表明，与陌生人进行短暂的交谈能使情绪得到明显的改善。但我们大多数人都不愿意开启这些对话，因为我们以为情况恰恰相反。

transcript.text: In an experiment, commuters who talked to nearby strangers found their commute more enjoyable than those who didn't. They were asked to predict whether they'd enjoy the commute more if they conversed with other people. Intriguingly, most expected the more solitary experience to be more pleasurable.
transcript.zh: 在一项实验中，与身边的陌生人交谈的通勤者发现，他们的通勤过程比那些没有交谈的人更令人愉快。他们被要求预测如果与他人交谈，自己是否会更享受通勤。有趣的是，大多数人预想独处的体验会更令人愉快。

transcript.text: Why is this? Social anxiety appears to be the problem. People's reluctance to start conversations with nearby strangers comes partly from "underestimating others' interest in connecting". The sad thing is that people presume that a nearby stranger doesn't want to converse and don't start a conversation. Only those who forced themselves to chat because it was required by the experiment found out what a pleasant experience it could be.
transcript.zh: 为什么会这样？社交焦虑似乎是问题所在。人们不愿意与身边的陌生人开启对话，部分原因在于“低估了他人建立联系的兴趣”。令人遗憾的是，人们假定身边的陌生人不想交谈，因而没有开启对话。只有那些因实验要求而强迫自己聊天的人，才发现这会是多么令人愉快的体验。

transcript.text: Human beings are social animals. Those who misunderstand the impact of social interactions may not, in some contexts, be social enough for their own well-being. You should be chatting with the strangers you encounter. You may occasionally have a negative encounter that might stick in your memory. This is because the human brain is biased to dwell on negative events. But starting conversations with strangers is still well worth the risk of rejection.
transcript.zh: 人类是社交动物。那些误解社交互动影响的人，在某些情况下可能为了自身的幸福感而表现得不够合群。你应该与遇到的陌生人聊天。你偶尔可能会遇到不愉快的经历，并且可能会留在记忆中。这是因为人类大脑倾向于关注负面事件。但冒着被拒绝的风险与陌生人开启对话依然非常值得。

transcript.text: It may surprise you that conversing with strangers will make them happier too. The pleasure of connection seems contagious. People who are talked to have equally positive experiences as those who initiate a conversation.
transcript.zh: 与陌生人交谈也会让他们感到更高兴，这可能会让你感到惊讶。建立联系的乐趣似乎具有传染性。被搭话的人与发起对话的人拥有同样积极的体验。

transcript.text: The Caribbean islands are divided into two worlds, a rich one and a poor one. This tropical region's economy is based mainly on farming. Farmers are of two types. One is the plantation owner who may have hundreds of thousands of acres. In contrast, the small cultivator is working only a few acres of land. Most visitors to the Caribbean are rich, like the plantation owner. They do not realize or do not want to realize that many farm families barely managed to get by on what they grow.
transcript.zh: 加勒比海诸岛被分为两个世界：一个富裕的世界和一个贫困的世界。这个热带地区的经济主要以农业为基础。农民有两种类型。一种是拥有数十万英亩土地的种植园主。相比之下，小农只耕种几英亩土地。大多数到加勒比海旅游的游客都很富有，就像种植园主一样。他们没有意识到，或者不愿意识到，许多农民家庭仅靠自己种植的东西勉强维持生计。

transcript.text: The Caribbean produces many things. Sugar is the main product. Other export crops are tobacco, coffee, bananas, spices and citrus fruits, such as orange, lemon or grapefruit. From the West Indies also come oil, mineral pitch and many forest products. Jamaica's aluminum ore supplies are the world's largest. Oil comes from Trinidad, Aruba and Curacao. But for many of the smaller islands, sugar is the only export. Rum, a strong alcoholic drink, which is distilled from sugar cane, is also an export. The world's best rum comes from this area. Local kinds vary from the light rums of Puerto Rico to the heavier darker rums of Barbados and Jamaica. American tourists enjoy stocking up on inexpensive high quality Caribbean rum while they're on vacation. In Curacao, the well-known liquor of that name is made from the thick outer skin of a native orange.
transcript.zh: 加勒比海地区生产许多东西。糖是主要产品。其他出口作物包括烟草、咖啡、香蕉、香料和柑橘类水果，如橙子、柠檬或葡萄柚。西印度群岛还出产石油、矿物沥青和许多林产品。牙买加的铝矿储量居世界首位。石油产自特立尼达、阿鲁巴和库拉索。但对许多较小的岛屿来说，糖是唯一的出口产品。朗姆酒是一种从甘蔗中蒸馏出来的烈性酒，也是一种出口产品。世界上最好的朗姆酒产自这一地区。当地朗姆酒的种类各不相同，从波多黎各的淡色朗姆酒，到巴巴多斯和牙买加较为浓烈、颜色较深的朗姆酒都有。美国游客在度假期间喜欢购买价格低廉而品质优良的加勒比朗姆酒。在库拉索，以该地闻名的酒名命名的利口酒，是用当地一种橙子的厚外皮制成的。

transcript.text: Ever since America's colonial days, the Caribbean islands have been favorite places to visit. Since World War II, tourism has increased rapidly. Because great numbers of people go there, the islanders have built elaborate resorts, developed harbors and airfields, improved the beaches and have expanded sea and air routes. Everything is at the resort-hotel, beach, shopping and recreation. The vacationer never has any reason to explore the island.
transcript.zh: 自美国殖民时期以来，加勒比海诸岛一直是人们喜爱的旅游地。第二次世界大战以来，旅游业迅速发展。由于前往那里的人数众多，岛民修建了精致的度假胜地，开发了港口和机场，改善了海滩，并扩展了海上和空中航线。度假酒店、海滩、购物和娱乐一应俱全。度假者完全没有理由去探索这座岛屿。

transcript.text: As in most places, those who have money live well indeed. Those who don't have money live at various levels of poverty. But here the poor greatly outnumber the wealthy. A visitor will find rich people living in apartments or Spanish houses at the seaside or in the countryside. Their servants might include a cook, a maid, and a nurse for their children. Most of the people live well below the poverty level. In towns, they live crowded together in tiny houses. Islanders make the best they can of what they have. Their homes are quite shabby. Sadly, most tourists never see the side of the Caribbean.
transcript.zh: 和大多数地方一样，有钱人确实过着优裕的生活。没有钱的人则处于不同程度的贫困之中。但在这里，穷人的数量远远超过富人。游客会看到富人住在海边或乡间的公寓里，或者住在西班牙式房屋中。他们的仆人可能包括厨师、女佣和照顾孩子的护士。大多数人的生活水平远低于贫困线。在城镇里，他们拥挤地住在狭小的房屋中。岛民们尽可能利用自己所拥有的一切。他们的住房相当破旧。令人遗憾的是，大多数游客从未见过加勒比海的这一面。

transcript.text: Talk to anyone who is a generation or two older, and they would most likely comment that children are more spoiled these days. No one wants to have or be around demanding, selfish and spoiled children, those who get bad-tempered or silently brood when they are not given everything they want immediately. Paradoxically, the parents of such children encourage this demanding behavior in the mistaken belief that by giving their children everything they can their children will be happy. In the short term, perhaps they are right. But in the longer term, such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied and resentful of the parents who tried so hard to please them.
transcript.zh: 和比自己年长一两代的人交谈，他们很可能会说，如今的孩子更加娇生惯养了。没有人愿意拥有或和那些要求过多、自私且被宠坏的孩子相处；当他们不能立即得到自己想要的一切时，就会变得脾气暴躁或闷闷不乐。矛盾的是，这类孩子的父母却错误地认为，只要尽可能满足孩子的一切要求，孩子就会感到幸福，于是反而助长了这种索取无度的行为。短期来看，他们或许是对的。但从长远来看，这些孩子最终会变得孤独、依赖他人、长期不满，并对那些竭力取悦他们的父母心怀怨恨。

transcript.text: Undoubtedly parents want to raise happy children who are confident, capable and likable rather than spoiled and miserable. One factor hindering this is that parents can't or don't spend enough quality time with their kids, and substitute this deficit with toys, games, gadgets and the like. Rather than getting material things, children need parents' devoted attention. The quantity of time spent together is less important than the content of that time. Instead of instantly satisfying their wishes, parents should help them work out a plan to earn things they'd like to have. This teaches them to value the effort as well as what it achieves.
transcript.zh: 毫无疑问，父母都希望把孩子培养成幸福、自信、有能力且讨人喜欢的人，而不是被宠坏又不快乐的人。阻碍这一目标的一个因素是，父母无法或没有花足够的高质量时间陪伴孩子，于是用玩具、游戏、电子设备之类的东西来弥补这一不足。孩子需要的不是物质上的东西，而是父母全心全意的关注。共同相处的时间长短并不如相处时光的内容重要。父母不应立即满足孩子的愿望，而应帮助他们制定计划，通过努力获得自己想要的东西。这能教会他们既重视努力本身，也重视努力所取得的成果。

transcript.text: Allow them to enjoy anticipation. Numerous psychological studies have demonstrated that children who learn to wait for things they desire are more likely to succeed in a number of ways later in life. One famous experiment in the 1960s involved 3- to 6-year-old children. They were given a choice between receiving a small reward, such as a cookie, immediately, or if they waited 15 minutes, they could have two. Follow up studies have found that those who chose to delay satisfaction are now more academically successful, have greater self-worth, and even tend to be healthier.
transcript.zh: 让孩子享受期待的过程。大量心理学研究表明，学会等待自己渴望的事物的孩子，日后更有可能在许多方面取得成功。20世纪60年代进行的一项著名实验以3至6岁的儿童为对象。他们可以选择立即得到一份小奖励，例如一块饼干；也可以等待15分钟，这样就能得到两块。后续研究发现，那些选择延迟满足的孩子，如今在学业上更加成功，自我价值感更强，而且往往也更加健康。

transcript.text: If they fail, children should be encouraged to keep trying rather than to give up if they really want the desired result. This teaches them how to handle and recover from disappointment, which is associated with greater success and satisfaction academically, financially and in personal relationships.
transcript.zh: 如果失败了，只要孩子确实想要达到预期的结果，就应鼓励他们继续尝试，而不是放弃。这能教会他们如何应对失望并从中恢复，而这与他们在学业、经济状况和个人关系方面取得更大的成功与满足感有关。

transcript.text: And lastly, parents should encourage their children to look at life from other points of view, as well as their own. This teaches them to be understanding of and sympathetic towards others—qualities sure to take them a long way in life.
transcript.zh: 最后，父母还应鼓励孩子从其他人的角度以及自己的角度看待生活。这能教会他们理解和同情他人，而这些品质必将让他们在人生道路上受益匪浅。

questions.stem: What will happen to children if they always get immediate satisfaction?

options.text: They will be more demanding of their next generation.
They will end up lonely, dependent and dissatisfied.
They will experience more setbacks than successes.
They will find it difficult to get along with others.

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确有 demanding, selfish and spoiled children 里的 demanding，A 用 more demanding of their next generation 把这个原词搬来，但录音说的是孩子本身"难缠"，不是说他们将来"对下一代更苛求"，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C 说孩子会经历 more setbacks than successes，但录音第1段讲长远后果时只提孤独、依赖、不满，从未说"挫折多于成功"，这是录音未提及的内容。
optionAnalysis.D: 过度推断：D 的 difficult to get along with others 看似贴近"孤独"，但录音长远后果那句只说 lonely / dependent / dissatisfied / resentful，并未说"难以与人相处"，是从 lonely 过度推断出来的，原话没这层意思。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（such children end up lonely, dependent, chronically dissatisfied ↔ They will end up lonely, dependent and dissatisfied. 近乎照搬但删了 chronically）

transcript.text: It is not hard to mess up an interview. Most people feel nervous sitting across from a hiring manager, answering questions that effectively open themselves up for judgment. And your chances of being more carefully considered for the job can quickly go downhill just by saying the wrong thing at the wrong time.
transcript.zh: 面试出错并不难。大多数人坐在招聘经理对面，回答那些实际上会让自己暴露在评判之下的问题时，都会感到紧张。仅仅因为在错误的时间说了错误的话，你被更认真地考虑录用的机会就可能迅速下降。

transcript.text: The most obvious thing not to do is complain. Employers want to hire positive people. Talking about a previous job negatively raises concerns that you might be difficult to manage, or you might be someone that blames management for your own poor performance.
transcript.zh: 最明显应该避免的事情就是抱怨。雇主希望招聘积极乐观的人。负面谈论上一份工作会引发担忧，让人觉得你可能难以管理，或者你可能是那种把自己的糟糕表现归咎于管理层的人。

transcript.text: Don't say that you've moved around in jobs because you haven't found the right fit or feel that you were not challenged enough. Statements like these will make you sound aimless and lost. An interviewer may well think, why would this role be any different for you? You will probably leave here in six months. It also begs the question of what type of relationship you had with your manager. It doesn't sound like you had open communication with him or her. Managers usually love people who can self-sustain and enable growth through taking initiative, who are strong at following through their work, and who bring ideas and solutions to the table.
transcript.zh: 不要说你换过多份工作是因为一直没有找到合适的岗位，或者觉得自己没有得到足够的挑战。这样的说法会让你听起来漫无目的、迷失方向。面试官很可能会想：这个职位对你来说又会有什么不同呢？你大概六个月后就会离开这里。这也会让人不禁思考你和经理之间的关系如何。听起来，你似乎没有与他或她进行坦诚的沟通。经理通常很喜欢那些能够自我驱动、通过主动采取行动促进成长、善于把工作贯彻到底，并且能够提出想法和解决方案的人。

transcript.text: If you were in a management or leadership position, when discussing your current role, never take all the credit for accomplishments or achievements. Emphasize your team and how through their talents, your vision was realized. Most successful leaders know that they are only as good as their team. And acknowledging this in an interview will go a long way towards suggesting that you might be the right person for the position you are applying for.
transcript.zh: 如果你曾担任管理或领导职位，在谈论当前职位时，绝不要把所有功劳或成就都归于自己。要突出你的团队，以及你是如何凭借他们的才能实现自己的愿景的。大多数成功的领导者都知道，自己的能力取决于团队的表现。在面试中承认这一点，将大大有助于表明你可能正是所申请职位的合适人选。

transcript.text: Lastly, have a good idea of what your role will be and try and convey the idea that you're flexible. Asking what your role will be suggests you will limit yourself purely to what is expected of you. In reality, your role is whatever you make of it. This is especially true in small companies, where the ability to adapt and take on new responsibilities is highly valued. And this is equally important if you're just starting out. Entry level interviewees would do well to demonstrate a broad set of skills in most interviews. It's important to have a wide skill set as many startups and small companies are moving really fast. Employers are looking for candidates that are intelligent and can quickly adapt and excel in a growing company.
transcript.zh: 最后，要清楚了解自己的职责，并努力传达出你具有灵活性。询问自己的职责是什么，会让人觉得你打算把自己严格限制在他人对你的期望之内。实际上，你的职责取决于你如何发挥。在小公司中尤其如此，因为适应变化并承担新的责任的能力备受重视。如果你刚刚开始职业生涯，这一点同样重要。对于初级职位的面试者来说，在大多数面试中展示广泛的技能组合会很有帮助。拥有多方面的技能非常重要，因为许多初创公司和小公司发展得非常快。雇主正在寻找聪明、能够迅速适应并在不断成长的公司中取得优异表现的候选人。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Last week, Burberry's annual report revealed that £28.6 million worth of stock was burnt last year. The news has left investors and consumers outraged but comes as little surprise to those in the fashion industry.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The practice of destroying unsold stock, and even rolls of unused fabric, is commonplace for luxury labels. Becoming too widely available at a cheaper price through discount stores discourages full-price sales. Sending products for recycling leaves them vulnerable to being stolen and sold on the black market. Jasmine Bina, CEO of brand strategy agency Concept Bureau explains, "Typically, luxury brands rally around exclusivity to protect their business interests, namely intellectual property and preservation of brand equity(资产)." She stated she had heard rumors of stock burning but not specific cases until this week.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Another reason for the commonplace practice is a financial incentive for brands exporting goods to America. United States Customs states that if imported merchandise is unused and destroyed under their supervision, 99% of the duties, taxes or fees paid on the merchandise may be recovered. It is incredibly difficult to calculate how much dead stock currently goes to waste. While there are incentives to do it, there's no legal obligation to report it.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A source, who chose to remain anonymous, shared her experience working in a Burberry store in New York in October 2016. "My job was to toss items in boxes so they could be sent to be burned. It was killing me inside because all that leather and fur went to waste and animals had died for nothing. I couldn't stay there any longer, their business practices threw me off the roof." In May this year, Burberry announced it was taking fur out of its catwalk shows and reviewing its use elsewhere in the business. "Even though we asked the management, they refused to give us detailed answers as to why they would do this with their collection," continued the source, who left her role within two weeks. She has since worked with another high-profile, luxury label.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: In an online forum post, which asked if it's true that Louis Vuitton burned its bags, Ahmed Bouchfaa, who claimed to work for Louis Vuitton, responded that the brand holds sales of old stock for staff members twice a year. Items which have still not sold after several sales are destroyed. "Louis Vuitton doesn't have public sales. They either sell a product at a given price or discontinue it. This is to make sure that everybody pays the same price for an item," he says. He goes on to disclose the strict guidelines around the employee sales: "You may buy gifts for someone, but they track each item, and if your gift ends up online they know who to ask." One investor commenting on the Burberry figures was reportedly outraged that the unsold goods were not even offered to investors before they were destroyed.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Richemont, who owns several luxury brands, hit the headlines in May for taking back £437 million of watches for destruction in the last two years to avoid marked-down prices. It's not just luxury brands either. In October last year, a Danish TV show exposed H&M for burning 12 tonnes of unsold clothing since 2013. In a statement, the high street retailer defended itself by saying that the burnt clothing had failed safety tests: "The products to which the media are referring have been tested in external laboratories. The test results show that one of the products is mold infested and the other product contains levels of lead that are too high. Those products have rightly been stopped in accordance with our safety routines." In March, a report revealed that H&M was struggling with $4.3 billion worth of unsold stock. The brand told The New York Times that the plan was to reduce prices to move the stock, arguably encouraging consumers to buy and throw away with little thought.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Over-production is perhaps the biggest concern for Burberry. While there has been much outrage at the elitist connotation of burning goods rather than making them affordable, executives at the British fashion house are no doubt struggling to defend how they miscalculated production. The waste has been put down to burning old cosmetic stock to make way for their new beauty range. However, while the value of destroyed stock is up from £26.9 million last year, it's an even more significant increase from 2016's figure of £18.8 million, highlighting that this is an ongoing issue.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: In September 2016, Burberry switched to a "see now, buy now" catwalk show format. The move was a switch to leverage on the coverage of their fashion week show to make stock available immediately to consumers. This is opposed to the traditional format of presenting to the industry, taking orders for production and becoming available in six months' time. While Burberry announced "record-breaking" online reach and engagement, there has been little evidence to suggest that the strategy has had a significant effect on sales, particularly as the hype(炒作) slows across the season. In February they made adjustments to the format, dropping some catwalk items immediately and promising that others would launch in the coming months.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: In a statement, Burberry denied that switching to "see now, buy now" has had an impact on waste. A Burberry spokesperson further said, "On the occasions when disposal of products is necessary, we do so in a responsible manner. We are always seeking ways to reduce and revalue our waste. This is a core part of our strategy and we have forged partnerships and committed support to innovative organizations to help reach this goal."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: One such partnership is with Elvis & Kresse, an accessories brand working with reclaimed materials. Co-founder Kresse Wesling said, "Late last year we launched an ambitious five-year partnership with the Burberry Foundation. The main aim of this is to scale our leather rescue project, starting with off-cuts from the production of Burberry leather goods. We are working tirelessly to expand our solutions and would love to welcome anyone to our workshop to come and see what we are doing." At the moment, the partnership only addresses waste at the production stage and not unsold goods.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: While these are honorable schemes, it makes it harder for Burberry to defend these latest figures. Fifteen years ago, Burberry was at crisis point as their signature check pattern was widely imitated by cheap, imitation brands. It deterred luxury consumers who found their expensive clothing more closely associated with working-class youth culture than a prestigious heritage fashion house. In the year 2004, at the height of over-exposure of the Burberry check, the brand's turnover was £715.5 million. Under Christopher Bailey as creative director they turned the brand around and this past year revenue hit £2.73 billion.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Bina believes that brands need to readdress their exclusivity tactic. "Exclusivity is starting to be challenged," she says, "I think that goes hand in hand with how luxury itself is being challenged. Access to fashion, and the brands who police it, are becoming less and less relevant. Things like health, enlightenment, and social and environmental responsibility are the new luxuries. These all come from within, not without. That's the challenge that traditional luxury brands will have to contend with in the mid- to long-term future."

Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and countless other social channels provide a quick and simple way to glimpse into a job candidate's personal life—both the positive and negative sides of it. Social media screening is tempting to use as part of the hiring process, but should employers make use of it when researching a potential candidate's background?

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Incorporating the use of social media to screen job candidates is not an uncommon practice. A 2018 survey found that almost 70% of employers use social media to screen candidates before hiring them. But there are consequences and potential legal risks involved too. When done inappropriately, social media screening can be considered unethical or even illegal.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Social media screening is essentially scrutinising a job candidate's private life. It can reveal information about protected characteristics like age, race, nationality, disability, gender, religion, etc., and that could bias a hiring decision.
